nodes.title: Commutator of lifts
nodes.statement: For a central GroupExtension A E G, commuting x,y∈G, and arbitrary lifts X,Y∈E, define κ_E(x,y)∈A by inl(κ_E(x,y))=XYX⁻¹Y⁻¹. Surjectivity supplies lifts, exactness gives kernel membership, and injectivity supplies a unique preimage. Centrality means inl(A)⊆Z(E).
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Use exactness to extract a kernel element; differences between lifts lie in the central kernel.
acceptance: In the split direct-product extension A×G→G, κ_E(x,y)=1 for every commuting pair.
For either D₈→C₂² or Q₈→C₂², lifts of two independent basis elements have commutator equal to the nonidentity central element.

nodes.title: The oriented commuting-pair cycle
nodes.statement: For xy=yx, [x|y]−[y|x] with integral coefficient 1 belongs to groupHomology.cycles₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ). The orientation is x followed by y.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: The existing d₂₁ sends [x|y] to [y]−[xy]+[x]; subtract the reversed formula and use xy=yx.
acceptance: Reversing the pair negates the cycle; the coefficient is 1, not 0.

nodes.title: Universal homological commutator
nodes.statement: For commuting x,y∈G define ⟨x,y⟩ as H2π applied to the oriented cycle [x|y]−[y|x], in M(G)=H₂(G,ℤ). Equivalently it is the image of the oriented generator of H₂(ℤ²,ℤ) under (a,b)↦xᵃyᵇ.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Use the existing cycle quotient. The comparison with the ℤ² generator and the UCT evaluation is an explicit homological supplier obligation.
acceptance: ⟨1,y⟩=0, since the displayed cycle is a boundary.
For G=C₂² and independent x,y, ⟨x,y⟩ is the nonzero element of M(G)≅C₂.
For G=ℤ² the ordered basis gives the positive generator; swapping gives its negative, not the same integer.

nodes.statement: For conjugacy-invariant c⊆G set Q_c to the additive subgroup of M(G) generated by ⟨x,y⟩ with x∈c and y∈C_G(x). No generation or rationality hypothesis on c is needed for this quotient.

nodes.title: Reduced Schur cover
nodes.statement: Given a chosen ordinary Schur cover π:S→G and its oriented class isomorphism τ_S:M(G)≅kerπ, define S_c=S/τ_S(Q_c). Retain π, τ_S and the cover choice as parameters. The descended π_c:S_c→G is a central surjection with kernel canonically identified with M(G,c) for these data.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Quotient by the central image of Q_c; descend the projection and use exactness to identify its kernel.
acceptance: For c=∅ the quotient is the chosen S itself.
For G=C₂² and c all nonidentity elements, either D₈ or Q₈ reduces to G.
For c=∅ the two reduced covers D₈ and Q₈ of C₂² are nonisomorphic: there is no canonical reduced extension determined by G,c.

nodes.title: Conjugacy classes lift bijectively
nodes.statement: Every conjugacy class in S_c with image contained in c∪{1} maps bijectively to its image conjugacy class in G. No uniqueness is asserted for which class above a class of c is chosen.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Surjectivity follows by lifting conjugators; two conjugators with equal image on x differ by a centralizer lift, which fixes X. Kernel elements are central singletons.
acceptance: Several classes above one class can exist, each individually mapping bijectively.

nodes.title: Marked central extension
nodes.statement: For conjugacy-invariant generating c⊆G, a c-marked central extension is a GroupExtension A E G with central kernel and a section s:c→E such that s(gxg⁻¹)=e s(x)e⁻¹ whenever π(e)=g. Its marked subset s(c) maps bijectively to c. A morphism is a group homomorphism over G preserving s; a kernel identification need not be fixed.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Bundle an existing extension together with marking data and genuine centrality/equivariance conditions.
acceptance: For G=1,c=∅, any central extension A→A→1 has the empty marking.
The identity extension G→G has its inclusion marking.
The quotient C₄→C₂ is marked on its nontrivial class using a lift of order 4; the marking is a set-section, not a splitting homomorphism.

nodes.title: Marking-preserving splitting correction
nodes.statement: Suppose φ:P→E is a homomorphism over G and φ(x̂,e_[x])=s(x)k_x with k_x∈A. The discrepancy depends only on [x]. Let ψ:P→A be the homomorphism factoring through deg:P→ℤ^D with ψ(e_[x])=k_x. Define φ_corr(p)=φ(p) inl(ψ(p))⁻¹.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Centrality makes the product a homomorphism; the free-degree universal property constructs ψ; cancel the discrepancy with its inverse.
acceptance: If all k_x=1 then φ_corr=φ.
In an additive C₃ kernel with discrepancy 1, subtraction gives 0 while addition gives 2.
Multiplying φ by ψ instead sends a marked point to s(x)k_x² and fails for a kernel element of order 3.

nodes.title: Finite power action
nodes.statement: Let G be finite, p prime with p∤|G| (or characteristic zero). A unit α of the prime-to-p profinite integers acts on the underlying set of G by g↦g^a, where a is its coordinate modulo ord(g). This is independent of the integer representative and factors through units modulo any positive common exponent of G.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Integer powers depend only on order; invertible residues supply inverse permutations. Centrality is not needed for the set permutation, but multiplicativity requires an abelian target.
acceptance: On C₃, the residue 2 interchanges the two nonidentity elements.
The trivial group has the trivial action.
In S₃, inversion (residue −1) fixes the transpositions (12),(23) but reverses their 3-cycle product, so it is not a group homomorphism.

nodes.title: Discrete cyclotomic action
nodes.statement: For P=S_c×_{G^ab}L define α*(h,m)=(h^α W_α(m),m^α). This defines a group action on the underlying set P, and hence on U through the marked comparison. Its projection to G is the ordinary power permutation and its degree projection is the class-degree permutation.
hypotheses: Use exactly the quantifiers and hypotheses in the statement; ambient conventions are pinned in the reader.
proofSteps: Check the fiber-product equality using δ compatibility; centrality permits raising h times a correction to a power. The correction cocycle proves identity and composition.
acceptance: The identity unit acts identically and all units fix 1_U.
For U(C₂,c)≅ℤ, the action is trivial because its generator and its unique class are fixed after correction.

nodes.statement: For commuting x,y, the homological commutator is additive in each commuting cyclic variable: ⟨x^n,y⟩=n⟨x,y⟩. In particular if x is an involution then 2⟨x,y⟩=0.
